messages.task:
You are a large-language-model financial analyst asked to reason over an excerpt from a bank’s Management Discussion & Analysis (MD&A).  You have access to a set of callable tools that expose certain data from an internal database.  Use them whenever they help you reach an answer that can be verified.

Scenario
The MD&A describes how the firm sets aside liquidity to meet potential collateral or termination payments that counterparties could demand if the firm’s long-term credit ratings were downgraded.  Management quantifies, for each year-end reporting date, the additional collateral or termination payments that could have been called in the event of both a one-notch and a two-notch downgrade.  These figures are assessed across the major rating agencies (for example, Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s).  The discussion also notes that collateral calls under bilateral agreements are driven by agency downgrades, that multiple agencies may act independently, and that the firm therefore analyses the aggregate impact of simultaneous downgrades.

Available tools
• list_major_rating_agencies() → list[str]
  Returns the names of rating agencies considered “major”.

• list_all_rating_agencies() → list[str]
  Returns the names of every agency in the database, including any that may not be material.

• list_available_years() → list[int]
  Gives the set of reporting years for which downgrade impact data exist.

• get_collateral_payment_for_agency(year: int, agency_name: str, notch_level: int) → int
  Provides the additional collateral or termination payment (in millions) that could have been called for a particular agency, year and downgrade severity (use 1 for a one-notch downgrade, 2 for a two-notch downgrade).

• get_total_collateral_payment_all_agencies(year: int, notch_level: int) → int
  Returns the aggregate collateral requirement across all agencies (major and non-major) for a given year and downgrade severity.

Question
What is the difference, in millions, between additional collateral or termination payments for a two-notch downgrade and those for a one-notch downgrade at the end of December 2012?

Instructions
Think step-by-step, decide which tools will help, call them as needed, perform any intermediate calculations, and finally respond with a single integer – the requested difference in millions – with no additional commentary.
